summary: You take three RELIGST courses numbered 1-99 (at most one Introductory Seminar), six numbered 100-289 (two at the 200 level), RELIGST 290, five units of RELIGST 297 for the senior essay or honors thesis and RELIGST 298, with more RELIGST courses making up the 60 units. At most 10 units (not counting RELIGST 298) may be S/NC or CR/NC. Approved language or other outside courses are moved in by hand, and the spread across religious traditions, transfer units, and the honors thesis and GPA are checked by hand.

u7yHmyTq-text.why: "The remainder of the coursework needed to bring the total Religious Studies unit count to 60 to be chosen according to interest, in consultation with the student's advisor, and with an eye to the senior capstone requirement." The same as rule ov-remaining (Remaining units in Religious Studies) and the 60-unit minimum.

XyvHDg0t.why: "Three courses (3-5 units each) from courses numbered RELIGST 1-99, only one of which may be an Introductory Seminar." The Introductory Seminars are the department's N and Q courses.

n9PAVAH5.why: "Six courses (4-5 units each) from courses numbered RELIGST 100-289, of which at least two must be at the 200-level."

ZoZmwnt2.why: "Senior Essay: five units, winter quarter ... Honors Thesis: five to ten units, spread over Autumn and Winter Quarters": at least 5 units of the repeatable RELIGST 297.

BesYRqpC.why: "The Honors Thesis is a 40-80 page research paper ... The Honors Thesis is read and graded by the student’s thesis advisor and another member of the Religious Studies faculty ... Theses earning a grade of ‘B+’ or above receive honors."
